**What you should be able to do after this meeting.** Present a plan somebody could pick up and execute in January. Know what your team owes AEM 6992 over the break.

## Where to read more

[Adams](https://doi.org/10.4135/9788132108498) ch. 15 on conducting your research, which is mostly about the months after this one.

## Session A · 2:00–3:15

Final presentations take the whole meeting, 2:00 to 4:30. Each of the nine teams has a 15-minute slot: 10 minutes to present, 4 minutes of questions from the room, and 1 minute to change over. Five teams present before a 10-minute break at 3:20. Present as you would in a seminar room, to an expert who is hearing your proposal for the first time and judging its importance, its soundness and its feasibility. It is recommended that every member of the team speaks. Each team reviews another team's work.

## Session B · 3:30–4:30

Every session B opens with a ten-minute team check-in: what you did
since last week, what is stuck, and who is doing what next. Written
down, and handed in with that session's work.

Final presentations continue with the last four teams, on the same clock: 10 minutes to present, 4 minutes of questions, 1 minute to change over.

Your team's output is submitted before you leave.

## Due

Final presentation, in class
